title: Console: Role & Access Quick-Filters and Inline Member Assignment
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, discoverable UI surface inside the Console Roles page that lets admins: 1) quickly filter roles by policy attributes (builtin vs custom, scope: org/team/project, privilege level), 2) preview permission summaries inline, and 3) assign or remove members from roles without leaving the list view. The goal is to reduce friction for common admin tasks and prevent mode-switching between list/detail pages for routine role adjustments.
problem_statement: Admin users frequently need to find roles with a specific scope or permission and then make a small member or binding change. Current console requires opening a role detail modal or page, which is slow for batch edits. This leads to admin friction, longer mean time to change, and an increased chance of stale role hygiene.
goals: Add multi-faceted quick-filters to the Roles list (scope, managed/builtin/custom, last-used, risky-permissions)
Allow in-list permission summary expansion for each role (compact read-only view)
Support inline member add/remove with role assignment preview and immediate audit note capture
Preserve discoverability for less-frequent actions (edit role, view audit history) by keeping those in detail view
non_goals: Redesigning the entire Roles page layout
Replacing existing advanced role-edit flows (these remain in role detail)
Creating a full RBAC policy language editor in-list
scope: This work covers the Roles list view and a small inline member assignment overlay. It includes visual design, interaction patterns, accessibility considerations, and handoff artifacts for implementation. Backend APIs for assignments and filters exist (ENG trackers) but minor API additions may be required.
out_of_scope: Audit log viewer changes, SSO provisioning flows, tenant-level policy creation UX remains in scope for separate tickets.
design_decisions: Inline assignment will be a transient overlay anchored to the role row, not a full page modal, to support fast repeated edits
Quick-filters are multi-select chips at the top of the Roles list with a persistent breadcrumb showing active filters
Permission summaries will use progressive disclosure: show top 3 high-impact permissions, expand to full list when requested
Changes made via inline assignment require a short required audit note to be entered before save to improve traceability
tradeoffs: Inline assignment overlay reduces context-switching but increases complexity in the list component—we limit features in the overlay to avoid bloat
Showing only top permissions improves scan speed but may hide less-frequent dangerous permissions; mitigation: add a clear 'risky permissions' filter and an expanded view
Requiring audit notes adds step friction but improves compliance; we will make the note short by default (3-250 chars) to balance speed and traceability
accessibility_considerations: Overlay will be keyboard-focus-trapped and announce role/context to screen readers
Filter chips will be reachable by keyboard and have aria-pressed states
Color usage will not rely on color alone; icons and labels used for status indicators
implementation_tasks: Design high-fidelity comps for desktop and tablet (Ava)
Create interaction spec with states and error handling (Ava)
Frontend implementation: list UI + overlay + keyboard handling (Priya)
Backend small API: batch member assignment endpoint + audit-note field (Omar)
Security review: permission-checking and audit retention (Marcus)
QA: accessibility checks and edge-case tests for filters + pagination
acceptance_criteria: Admins can apply at least 4 pre-defined quick-filters and combine them; list updates instantly
Each role row has an expand control to reveal top 3 permissions; clicking expands full permission list in-place
Clicking 'Manage members' on a role opens an inline overlay allowing add/remove of members and requires a short audit note before saving
All member changes created through this flow appear in the audit log with the provided note and show up in the Console's recent activity within 60s
Keyboard navigation and screen reader announcements meet WCAG 2.1 AA for the new UI pieces
Design handoff includes annotated Figma files, interaction spec, and a small token set for spacing/colors
open_questions: Should the overlay allow role binding to groups (SCIM/LDAP) in V1? Backend SCIM support exists but group UX may add complexity
Do we surface permission diffs when assigning a role to a member who already has overlapping permissions via another role?
What rate limits should apply to inline batch assignments to prevent accidental mass changes?
recent_updates: 2025-11-18: Ticket created by Ava Martinez. Initial problem statement and goals captured.
2025-11-21: Design spike completed; low-fidelity wireframes pasted to Figma (link in attachments). Decided to anchor overlay to row instead of a global modal.
2025-11-25: PM review (Jonah Kim): proposed filters approved; requested adding 'last-used' column to help cleanup scenarios.
2025-11-29: Security review (Marcus Boyd): audit note required; also asked for proof that backend audit retention supports notes up to 250 chars. Eng to confirm.
2025-12-03: Eng sync: Backend can add audit-note field in assignment API (ENG-4199). Priya started implementing keyboard focus handling. Updated ticket metadata and estimate.
2025-12-03: Accessibility review scheduled for 2025-12-05 with QA and Accessibility specialist.
review_feedback: Jonah Kim (PM) on 2025-11-25: Ask to include 'last-used' and 'assigned-by' columns in compact view for admin triage
Marcus Boyd (Security) on 2025-11-29: Mandatory audit note and ensure ACL checks performed server-side before assignment
Priya Nair (Frontend) on 2025-12-02: Suggests lazy-loading full permission list to avoid long render times for orgs with many roles
risks: Over-centralizing assignment actions could lead to accidental mass edits; mitigations: confirmation step for >10 changes, rate limits
Exposing permission summaries may surface complex permission sets that need more explanation; mitigations: contextual help and 'why this matters' tooltip
API coupling required for audit notes; if backend is delayed, we will fallback to opening detail page with the same required fields
